name: Level 3 Policy-Bounded Autonomous Code-Generation Agent
description: Extend the proven Level 2 supervised coding agent to complete longer, multi-step engineering tasks autonomously inside explicit policy and resource boundaries. Level 3 autonomy is conditional and auditable; it does not grant blanket authority to merge, release, deploy, or perform irreversible production actions.

metadata.autonomyDefinition: The agent can decompose and carry out eligible multi-step engineering tasks, adapt using repository and verification feedback, and deliver an evidence-backed candidate change without per-step approval when policy permits.
metadata.prerequisiteExitCriteria: All Phase 12 Level 2 exit criteria pass, including real editing, real checks, approval controls, persistence, and cross-interface acceptance.
nonGoals: No unrestricted network, shell, filesystem, or credential access
No autonomous production deployment, protected-branch merge, release publication, or secrets rotation
No claiming autonomous competence beyond measured task and repository classes

tasks.name: Define Level 3 autonomy profiles and policy boundaries
deliverables: Define disabled, supervised, and policy-bounded autonomy profiles with explicit allowed actions
Create a risk matrix for file edits, dependency changes, generated code, tests, network access, and Git operations
Set hard maximums for task duration, changed files, repair attempts, model cost, and tool calls
Specify mandatory escalation and human-approval conditions
acceptanceCriteria: Unknown or missing policy settings resolve to the least autonomous behavior
Protected, irreversible, or production actions cannot be enabled by a task prompt
Policy decisions have machine-readable reasons and audit records

tasks.name: Plan long-horizon engineering work as a dependency graph
deliverables: Decompose eligible requests into bounded tasks with explicit dependencies, outcomes, and per-task budgets
Execute ready tasks in dependency order with configurable, workspace-safe concurrency
Replan only from recorded evidence and require approval when scope or risk materially increases
Expose graph progress, blocked tasks, and remaining budget
acceptanceCriteria: Cycles, missing prerequisites, and unbounded decomposition are rejected
A failed prerequisite prevents dependent changes from being reported complete
Replanning preserves completed evidence and never silently broadens approved scope

tasks.name: Add durable resumable autonomous-run state
deliverables: Persist dependency graph state, budgets, policy version, context provenance, decisions, and verification evidence
Resume eligible runs after process interruption with lease and duplicate-execution protection
Revalidate workspace state, approvals, tool availability, and remaining budgets before resuming
Support explicit pause, resume, cancel, and operator takeover
acceptanceCriteria: Restart and duplicate-request tests do not repeat completed writes or exceed task budgets
Policy changes invalidate incompatible checkpoints and require explicit reconciliation
Operator takeover prevents background work from mutating files afterward

tasks.name: Build repository-level architecture and dependency context
deliverables: Build an incremental repository map of modules, entry points, tests, configurations, and dependency boundaries
Use available language analyzers and symbol references to support impact analysis
Track map freshness and invalidate affected context after edits
Explain file-selection rationale and uncertainty to the planner and reviewer
acceptanceCriteria: Stale or incomplete maps are detected and trigger refresh or a conservative scope
Impact analysis is tested against representative multi-module dependency fixtures
No private repository content is transmitted to a provider unless configured by the workspace policy

tasks.name: Select and expand verification based on change impact
deliverables: Map changed files and dependency impact to targeted tests, static checks, builds, and broader suites
Use changed-file tests for iteration and require configured final gates before completion
Detect when checks are skipped, flaky, unavailable, or provide insufficient evidence
Allow policy to require full suites or independent review for high-impact changes
acceptanceCriteria: The agent cannot equate a targeted test pass with all required final gates passing
Verification selection is reproducible from recorded change and policy inputs
Fixtures prove that dependency-impact changes expand verification scope

tasks.name: Isolate autonomous changes in transactional workspaces
deliverables: Run autonomous modifications in an isolated workspace or Git worktree without overwriting active user edits
Create checkpoints before each accepted patch batch and maintain a complete changed-file manifest
Provide rollback and discard operations with explicit confirmation and recovery logging
Compare the final candidate against the original base and detect unexpected files or generated artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent user edits to the source workspace are preserved
Cancellation, failed verification, and policy violation can safely discard or restore the isolated candidate
Isolation and recovery are tested on Windows, Linux, and macOS

tasks.name: Implement multi-stage self-repair with stop conditions
deliverables: Iterate plan, implement, test, inspect diff, and repair across dependent tasks
Track regressions and compare each repair against previous verification results
Stop on repeated failures, oscillating changes, security-sensitive behavior, uncertain requirements, or budget exhaustion
Produce a concise unresolved-issues report and candidate diff on early stop
acceptanceCriteria: Loop termination is deterministic under configured limits
Repeated or regressive patches cannot be accepted as progress
Stop and escalation conditions are covered by adversarial and fault-injection tests

tasks.name: Add policy-gated external quality and security checks
deliverables: Integrate configured CI, security scan, dependency, license, and performance checks as evidence providers
Define which checks can run automatically and which require credentialed or external-service access
Prevent secret-bearing output from being sent to models or attached to shared logs
Create evidence adapters that retain source, revision, timestamp, status, and check configuration
acceptanceCriteria: Unavailable or unauthorized checks are reported as incomplete, never passed
External-service operations require explicit workspace configuration and scoped credentials
Sensitive-output tests demonstrate redaction before persistence or model submission

tasks.name: Provide reproducible audit trail and autonomy telemetry
deliverables: Record policy version, task graph, context references, model/provider metadata, tool calls, approvals, diffs, checks, and stop reasons
Support deterministic export of an agent run for review without exporting secret values
Add local-first, privacy-controlled metrics for completion, regressions, escalations, and resource use
Make records queryable through existing CLI, API, and MCP group surfaces
acceptanceCriteria: An exported run can be reviewed to reconstruct the basis for every file mutation
Telemetry is opt-in where it leaves the workspace and remains local by default
Audit integrity and redaction have regression tests

tasks.name: Add escalation, takeover, and final human decision gates
deliverables: Escalate ambiguous requirements, policy conflicts, elevated risks, repeated failures, and scope changes to an operator
Provide pause and takeover controls across CLI, API, and MCP
Require human approval before publishing patches, merging protected branches, releases, or deployments
Ensure pending decisions expire safely without applying further changes
acceptanceCriteria: No prompt or generated plan can disable mandatory approval gates
Pause, takeover, timeout, and denied-approval tests prove no subsequent mutations
Every escalation includes evidence, options, and the exact pending action

tasks.name: Create autonomy quality, safety, and benchmark suite
deliverables: Build a versioned benchmark set of representative repository tasks with hidden acceptance checks
Measure task success, test regressions, unsafe actions, human escalations, resource use, and reproducibility
Add prompt-injection, malicious repository content, tool misuse, budget bypass, and checkpoint tampering scenarios
Set release thresholds and publish known capability limits by language and task class
acceptanceCriteria: Safety regressions block release regardless of aggregate task-success score
Benchmark results include exact agent, policy, model, and toolchain versions
No Level 3 capability is enabled by default without passing its documented thresholds

tasks.name: Validate Level 3 rollout and operational readiness
deliverables: Run staged pilot evaluations on disposable and opt-in repositories before broad availability
Document autonomy profiles, supported task classes, prerequisites, rollback, and incident response
Add feature flags and safe downgrade path to Level 2 supervised behavior
Require maintainer approval of benchmark evidence and operational go/no-go
acceptanceCriteria: Level 3 remains disabled unless explicitly enabled by workspace policy
Pilot users can stop, inspect, and discard an agent candidate at any time
Rollout is blocked by unmet safety thresholds, unresolved critical UAT issues, or absent maintainer approval

exitCriteria: All Level 2 capabilities and safety gates from Phase 12 remain passing
Eligible multi-step tasks can be completed within explicitly configured policy and resource budgets
All changes are isolated, reviewable, recoverable, and supported by real verification evidence
Mandatory escalation and human approval remain in force for protected and consequential actions
Versioned quality and safety benchmarks meet approved release thresholds
Level 3 rollout receives explicit maintainer go/no-go approval
